requirements.text: For each of the 80 live baseline rules (81 (capability, BR id) pairs minus the retired L1-posting/BR-009), the same HTTP request against the Python build at e1fbd3a and the Rust build, each on its own copy of the same database, returns the same status code and the same response body after agreed normalisation (generated ids, timestamps, token values)
requirements.how: Black-box parity suite in minidon-rust that starts either build as a process and runs the same test cases against it; a test counts only after it passes against Python
requirements.source: ticket.md ## Acceptance (parity test per rule); denominator from research/inputs/human-decisions.md ## 1; the dual-target harness is DERIVED

requirements.text: The Rust build starts on a SQLite database created and populated by the Python build and serves it with no migration; the Python build reads data written by the Rust build with the same results
requirements.how: Round-trip compatibility tests in CI: Python writes, Rust reads and writes, Python reads; includes enum columns (stored as upper-case member names such as 'ADMIN', 'PRIVATE'), naive UTC datetimes ('YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff'), password hashes and tokens
requirements.source: ticket.md ## Scope (same data) and ## Acceptance (no migration); the reverse direction and the format details are DERIVED (research-review-001 F-09 probe)

requirements.text: Error and edge responses match Python: the DomainError mapping (400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 429) with body {"error": msg}; request validation failures, which FastAPI returns as 422 with a different body {"detail": [...]}; unknown routes ({"detail": "Not Found"}) and wrong methods (405). Which framework-level details (for example the exact validation body, and whether /openapi.json, /docs and /redoc are contract) are part of the contract is decided in design (ADR candidate 3) and then tested
requirements.how: Differential run of a recorded request sequence covering all 40 endpoints against both builds, plus targeted parity tests, including 409 cases (username taken, email registered, already boosted, report already closed) and the 429 posting rate limit

requirements.text: Existing credentials keep working: accounts created by Python sign in on Rust, and access tokens issued by Python authenticate on Rust until they expire
requirements.how: Compatibility tests using accounts and tokens created through the Python API
requirements.source: ticket.md ## Scope (same data); baseline gate answer OQ-003 (hashing unchanged here, upgrade is a follow-up) in .mw/runs/BASELINE-2026-10-30/baseline-review-report.json

requirements.text: Time-dependent rules (60-minute edit window, 30 posts per rolling hour, 30-day token TTL, ordering by created_at) are tested at and around each boundary without real waiting, and the suite is deterministic (no flaky reruns)
requirements.how: Controlled clock in Rust, controlled data timestamps in the shared database file for the Python side (the Python code may not change); suite run 10 times in CI with no difference

requirements.text: Rust build quality: cargo fmt clean, cargo clippy with warnings denied, cargo test green, cargo audit and cargo deny clean, Cargo.lock committed
requirements.how: CI checks on every pull request to minidon-rust

requirements.text: Performance: no requirement. Performance parity is not requested and the Python build has no latency or throughput measurement
requirements.how: Not tested in this run. If the PO adds a requirement, measure the Python build first (research/inputs/baseline-metrics.md, Notes)

requirements.text: Under concurrent requests the Rust build does not fail where the Python build succeeds (for example SQLite 'database is locked' errors under parallel writes)
requirements.how: A small concurrent-write smoke test against both builds; differences recorded as risks, not as parity failures

requirements.text: Same configuration surface: MINIDON_DATABASE_URL (default sqlite:///./minidon.db), MINIDON_DOMAIN (default minidon.local), the Settings defaults (500-character status, 60-minute edit window, 30 posts per hour, 30-day token TTL), and a development entry point on 127.0.0.1:8000 (hard-coded in minidon/__main__.py:10)
requirements.how: Configuration parity test that starts the Rust build with and without each variable
requirements.source: minidon/config.py and minidon/__main__.py at e1fbd3a; GRD-007

requirements.text: Text-processing parity: mention and hashtag extraction, length limits, case folding and trimming give the same result as Python for every input, including non-ASCII input. Specifically: the mention and hashtag patterns behave like Python re with its lookbehinds and Unicode \w and \b; length limits (status plus spoiler 500, display name 30, bio 500, password minimum 8, report comment 1000) count Unicode code points, not bytes; usernames, emails and tags are lower-cased with Python's Unicode str.lower(); content and email are trimmed with Python's str.strip() whitespace set
requirements.how: Unicode inputs (accented letters, non-Latin scripts, emoji, combining marks, non-ASCII whitespace, @ and # next to word characters) are a required class in the parity suite for every rule that reads text; any regex engine choice is checked against this class
requirements.source: RISK-010; minidon/statuses/service.py:19-20, 70, 120, 229, 252; accounts/service.py:39-40, 45, 122, 126; moderation/service.py:28; timelines/service.py:85 at e1fbd3a

requirements.text: If the Rust build ever creates the schema on an empty database, the result matches what SQLAlchemy create_all produces for the Python build (table and column names, types, VARCHAR lengths, NOT NULL, unique constraints and indexes), so a fresh Rust-created database is readable by Python and the other way round
requirements.how: Schema comparison test: create an empty database with each build and compare sqlite_master; or decide in design that Rust never creates the schema and test that it refuses to
